lessons.title: From exchange antisymmetry to pairing representations
lessons.summary: First distinguish the spin, momentum and orbit indicators, and then understand why s and d waves are classified by symmetry.

sections.title: Exchanging two fermions must reverse the pairing amplitude
sections.text: The two spin indices of Δ belong to a pair of electrons. Exchange transposes them and reverses relative momentum k→−k. In this single-orbital, spin-rotation-symmetric model, the spin-singlet part is antisymmetric, requiring an even scalar momentum function. The spinless Kitaev chain instead uses odd-momentum pairing. Multiorbital or strong-SOC systems need explicit orbital indices and cannot simply inherit this simplified rule.

sections.title: uses square grid point group classification basis function
sections.text: Use orthogonal axes of a two-dimensional square lattice. Both a constant and cos kx+cos ky belong to A₁g; cos kx−cos ky belongs to B₁g and sin kx sin ky to B₂g, using D₄h even-parity labels. d+id combines B₁g and B₂g complexly and is not one two-dimensional irrep of this point group. Classification specifies transformation laws, not which pairing state wins in a material.

sections.title: Check the Hamiltonian in the full Nambu basis
sections.text: This module retains the electron up/down spin and corresponding holes to obtain a 4×4 BdG matrix. Its particle-hole symmetry comes from Nambu redundancy; it does not mean that the normal electron energy bands must be symmetric about the Fermi energy. Open the experiment to change the pairing function and check for Hermitian properties, exchange conditions, and particle–hole residuals. Δ₀ is an input parameter and does not solve the energy gap equation nor predict the critical temperature.

lessons.title: When does the energy gap zero line become a quasi-particle node?
lessons.summary: stacks the pairing function and the normal state Fermi surface together to avoid misjudgment of any Δ=0 position as a zero-energy excitation.

sections.title: First find the normal Fermi surface
sections.text: Nearest-neighbor square-lattice dispersion is set by hopping t and chemical potential μ. The color map shows the pairing function, while dark markers show the normal-state Fermi surface ξ=0. A superconducting zero-energy node must lie in both zero sets; for |μ|>4t, the normal state has no Fermi surface.

sections.title: gives the d-wave node an analytical position
sections.text: dₓ²₋ᵧ² is zero requirement cos kx=cos ky, and then combined with the Fermi surface equation. When t=1 and μ=−1, both are 1/4, and four symmetric nodes are obtained. The finite grid may not have exactly the nodes, and the total energy gap cannot be proved by using the minimum energy on the picture to be greater than zero. The module reports both analytical classification and numerical sampling results.

sections.title: Use counterexamples to understand the limits of label representation
sections.text: constant s-wave has a full energy gap at Δ₀≠0, but the extended s-wave belonging to A₁g is exactly zero on the entire Fermi surface when this model half-fills μ=0. Both parts of d+id must be zero at the same time to have a node. In this model of |μ|<4t, the full energy gap can be opened. Neither the total energy gap nor the pairing labels here are sufficient to determine the pairing mechanism of real materials on their own.

lessons.title: Kitaev chain: bulk gap and finite-system edge states
lessons.summary: connects odd parity pairings, bulk topological intervals, and open chain local weights to distinguish mathematical models from material evidence.

sections.title: A minimal spin-free paired chain
sections.text: Each site has one fermionic orbital. Nearest-neighbor pairing is odd in momentum, with sin k dependence, satisfying exchange antisymmetry. Inputs t,μ,Δ define the model; SOC, Zeeman fields, contacts and disorder of specific nanowires are absent, so this is not a quantitative prediction for an actual material.
sections.formula: ξ(k)=−2t cos k−μ；Δ(k)=2iΔ sin k；E±=±√[(2t cos k+μ)²+4Δ²sin²k]

sections.title: Locate phase boundaries from bulk gap closings
sections.text: For Δ≠0, the pairing vanishes at both k=0 and π, and the bulk gap closes at μ=−2t or +2t. In this single-channel chain, |μ|<2t is the nontrivial region and |μ|>2t is the trivial region. At Δ=0 the model generally returns to a metallic chain; a point without a bulk gap cannot be labeled a verified topological superconducting phase.

sections.title: Look at the boundary weight, not just near-zero energy
sections.text: With open boundaries, compare the electron-plus-hole weights of low-energy states and their dependence on chain length. The two ends of a finite chain can hybridize; near-zero-energy states are not exactly pinned to zero for arbitrary parameters. A BdG eigenvector should not be identified directly with an isolated Majorana. First check the bulk criterion, then inspect the mean spatial weight of the lowest two states and compare it with the trivial preset μ=3. This mean weight is invariant under a change of basis within the two-state subspace and sums to 1 over all sites.

lessons.title: Same-frequency second-order tensor: why 4mm has three coefficients
lessons.summary: separates the point group constraint from the frequency permutation symmetry to avoid mistaking the dynamic SHG for a static fully symmetric tensor.

sections.title: Write the output and input frequencies
sections.text: SHG Connect the two inputs of frequency ω to the polarization of 2ω. If the two inputs are the same, only the last two indicators j and k are guaranteed to be interchangeable; the frequency of the output indicator i is different and cannot be arbitrarily exchanged with j or k. Kleinman symmetry is discussed only if the corresponding approximation conditions are additionally met, and this module does not impose it.

sections.title: Find the allowed tensor using all point group operations
sections.text: The Td model of GaAs has only one independent coefficient, and the six xyz arrangements are equal; 4mm has three independent coefficients of xxz, zxx, and zzz. In particular, χ_xxz=χ_xzx=χ_yyz=χ_yzy and χ_zxx=χ_zyy are not bound to each other. The input was χ, not d=χ/2; the full index sum already includes factor 2 of the cross term.

sections.title: Using inversion to establish a zero response control
sections.text: A polar third-rank tensor changes sign under inversion, so bulk electric-dipole χ vanishes in centrosymmetric Oh. This applies only to the bulk electric-dipole contribution; surfaces and higher multipoles are outside the calculation. Use Oh as a limiting check rather than treating one zero-intensity curve as experimental proof of inversion.

lessons.title: From crystal section to four-channel angle spectrum
lessons.summary: Specifies the sample rotation, polarization letters and common intensity scale, and hand calculates a directly checkable GaAs pattern.

sections.title: Fix the laboratory scattering plane and rotate the sample
sections.text: The outward surface normal is +z, the scattering plane is xz and incidence angle θ is measured from the normal. The first letter denotes incident polarization and the second the analyzer, so PS means P incident/S outgoing. The sample rotates actively by φ about z. The (001)/(111) presets set initial orientation; for tetragonal (111), the normal also depends on c/a.

sections.title: Add amplitudes coherently, then take the squared modulus
sections.text: Transform the electric field into crystal coordinates, calculate nonlinear polarization, then project onto the outgoing analyzer. Complex coefficients interfere constructively or destructively; intensities of individual terms cannot be calculated and added first. All four curves share arbitrary units, so tripling every χ must multiply intensity by nine.

sections.title: Analytical check for GaAs (001)
sections.text: orders a=χ_xyz. The PP and SP channels are proportional to sin 2φ, PS is proportional to cos 2φ, and SS is zero. I_PP=1/8 when θ=45°, φ=45°, a=1. All channels are zero at θ=0, which is an example of geometric zero signals also occurring in non-centrosymmetric materials. Results do not include Fresnel, refraction, phase matching, or absolute optical power.
sections.formula: A_PP=−a cos²θ sinθ sin2φ；A_PS=2a cosθ sinθ cos2φ；A_SP=−a sinθ sin2φ；A_SS=0

lessons.title: Reverse reasoning: What can a SHG picture prove?
lessons.summary: uses global sign variation, unknown coefficients, and geometric extinction to train finite inference on experimental patterns.

sections.title: The same intensity can come from different complex amplitudes
sections.text: turns all χ into −χ at the same time, A will change sign, but |A|² will not change at all. The global complex phase also cannot be recovered from independent intensity maps. If the only difference between the two inverted polar domain is an overall χ change of sign, the current intensity demonstration cannot identify the positive and negative domains individually and would require a phase reference or other evidence.

sections.title: The rotational symmetry of the pattern is not equal to complete point group
sections.text: This geometric projection of a third-rank tensor for 4mm (001) is independent of φ, although the crystal has only fourfold rather than continuous rotation symmetry. Conversely, different tensors, cuts and coefficients may give similar four-lobed plots. Multiple channels and cuts add constraints but do not guarantee a unique answer without a specified model.
sections.formula: Observation pattern = point group Allowed tensor + coefficient + orientation + optical geometry

sections.title: Replace unique labels with falsifiable comparisons
sections.text: First write candidate point group and orientation, then explain which channels and angles can distinguish them; also check the influence of instrument background, surface contribution and Fresnel factor. This experiment supports coherence pattern comparison of complex coefficients and does not include experimental fits, confidence intervals, or automatic point group identification. It is recommended to save candidate inputs with complete results and record explanations that have not yet been ruled out.
sections.formula: a zero channel ≠ proven χ=0 ≠ proven material with inversion

lessons.title: supercell Why make the energy band denser?
lessons.summary: uses the complete chain as a control to separate Brillouin zone folding from true translation symmetry breaking .

sections.title: expands the real space cell and reduces the reciprocal space interval
sections.text: primitive cell The spacing is a=1, and N times the length of supercell is N. supercell wave number K is located at [−π/N,π/N), each K corresponds to N primitive cell momentum k=K+2πm/N, and finally folds back to primitive cell Brillouin zone . Momentum in the program uses radian wavenumbers; the plot axis k/π is the display coordinate, not the unit cell fractional coordinates .

sections.title: The same physical spectrum can be drawn into more branches
sections.text: The perfect chain retains primitive-cell translation symmetry; choosing a larger calculation cell does not change the physical Hamiltonian. A supercell plot has N folded branches, which do not imply new orbitals or a phase transition. The ideal single-orbital primitive dispersion remains ε₀−2t cos k.

sections.title: Let the spectral weight tell you the original momentum
sections.text: Unfolding retains supercell eigenenergies and calculates their projected weights at primitive Bloch momenta. Summed spectral weights of a perfect chain must recover one primitive-cell dispersion even if the solver mixes eigenvectors at degeneracies. Compare perfect and impurity presets to distinguish folding from actual Hamiltonian changes.

lessons.title: Where do spectral weights come from: phase, projection and summation rules
lessons.summary: Start with the hand calculations of N=2 and understand why eigenvalues cannot replace the wave function.

sections.title: Fixed supercell Bloch phase convention
sections.text: This tool uses ψ(RN+j)=exp(iKRN)c_j, where j is the primitive cell grid point retained in the cell. The intracellular phase exp(−ikj) must be preserved when projecting onto the primitive cell momentum. Directly weighting |c_j|² cannot recover the phase interference, and it is impossible to distinguish the momentum of the uniform state and the alternating state.

sections.title: hand calculation using two-site uniform state
sections.text: For N=2, K=0, c=(1,1)/√2 interferes constructively at k=0 and destructively at k=π, giving W(0)=1 and W(π)=0. Replacing it with (1,−1)/√2 exchanges these weights, although both states have identical real-space probabilities. Sitewise probabilities alone are therefore insufficient for unfolding.

sections.title: diagnostic implementation using conservation rules
sections.text: For a normalized eigenstate, weights summed over its N corresponding primitive momenta equal 1. In a complete N-orbital model, summing over every band at fixed k also gives 1. Actually removing orbitals and retaining M changes the latter to M/N; do not renormalize it away. Individual-state weights inside a degenerate subspace depend on basis, so compare weights summed over equal-energy states.

lessons.title: From defective teaching chain to real computing process
lessons.summary: Identify the boundaries between periodic defect arrays, finite models, and first principles expansions.

sections.title: Three different Hamiltonian changes
sections.text: The impurity preset changes one onsite potential; dimerization changes alternating-bond hopping; the alternating potential changes the two sublattices’ onsite energies. The vacancy preset actually removes an orbital and its connections. Every defect repeats with supercell periodicity, so an N=4 impurity chain is not an isolated infinitely dilute defect. Similar gaps do not uniquely identify mechanisms.

sections.title: Retain wavefunctions for actual VASP band unfolding
sections.text: Real 3D tasks require compatible references primitive cell and supercell , clear transformation relationships, corresponding supercell sampling points, and wave function output. WAVECAR can be processed locally using programs such as easyunfold and then checked for coordinate and symmetry conventions. The current calculator on this site only accepts the one-dimensional orthogonal single orbit eigenstate JSON, and will not automatically guess the limited information of POSCAR, EIGENVAL or PROCAR into general expansion weights.
sections.formula: structural relationship + K point + wave function/equivalent complete projection information → momentum spectrum weight

sections.title: Distinguish unfolded spectra from experimental photoemission intensity
sections.text: Unfolded weights measure Bloch character relative to a reference primitive cell, not ARPES intensity including photoemission matrix elements, detector resolution and surface effects. Imports require normalized complex eigenvectors, orbital positions and phase conventions; energies alone are rejected. Retain parameters, model limits and provenance when comparing concentrations or calculation settings.
sections.formula: Unfolding leaves E_n unchanged; it changes the displayed weight W_n(k) at each k

exercises.title: Pushing from Pauli conditions to square d-wave representation
exercises.prompt: Restrict to a single-orbital, spin-rotation-invariant spin singlet. Check exchange conditions, spatial parity, and fourfold rotation in order.

steps.prompt: After exchanging two electrons, which condition should the pairing matrix satisfy?
steps.hint: swap both transposes the two spin indicators and inverts the relative momentum.
steps.explanation: Fermion anticommutation requires Δ(k)=−Δᵀ(−k).

steps.prompt: The spin singlet matrix iσy is already antisymmetric, what is the parity of the scalar ψ(k)?
steps.hint: The total exchange sign must be negative.
choices: Arbitrary, nothing to do with exchange
steps.explanation: The antisymmetric spin part is multiplied by the even space part to obtain a total antisymmetric pairing.

steps.prompt: How does the fourfold rotation (kx,ky)→(−ky,kx) transform cos kx−cos ky?
steps.hint: Cosine is an even function, exchange x and y and then compare.
steps.explanation: cos(−ky)−cos kx=−(cos kx−cos ky), consistent with the B₁g basis function.

steps.prompt: In this D₄h model, how should dₓ²₋ᵧ²+i dₓᵧ be marked?
steps.hint: B₁g and B₂g are two different one-dimensional representations.
steps.explanation: The complex combination is not a single 2D irrep of the square lattice point group ; whether it forms spontaneously requires additional energetics information.

exercises.title: Find the four nodes at μ=−1 analytically
exercises.prompt: Take pairs t=1, Δ₀≠0, and dₓ²₋ᵧ² and use equations instead of graphical grids to determine zero-energy nodes.

steps.prompt: What does it take for E=√(ξ²+|ψ|²) to be zero?
steps.hint: For the sum of two non-negative terms to be zero, each term must be zero.
steps.explanation: The paired zero line must intersect the normal state Fermi surface to produce a quasiparticle zero energy node.

steps.prompt: What is the sum of cosines given by ξ=0 when μ=−1?
steps.hint: Move −2(cos kx+cos ky)+1=0 to the item.
steps.explanation: The normal Fermi surface satisfies cos kx+cos ky=1/2.

steps.prompt: Combined with the d-wave cos kx=cos ky, what do you get?
steps.hint: The sum of two identical numbers is 1/2.
steps.explanation: Each of kx and ky can be ±arccos(1/4), resulting in four nodes.

steps.prompt: The minimum energy of a finite grid is a small positive number. Can the above analytical node be overturned?
steps.hint: The grid does not necessarily contain arccos(1/4).
choices: Yes, numerical values ​​are always more reliable than analysis.
Yes, as long as the colormap is smooth enough
No, you need to check the sampling position or directly substitute it into the node
steps.explanation: The numerical grid may be missing zeros; analytical substitution and convergence checks are used for verification.

exercises.title: Examine bulk criteria together with boundary evidence
exercises.prompt: Use a Kitaev chain with t=1,Δ=0.6,μ=0.5; compare bulk spectra, open boundaries and finite-size effects.

steps.prompt: At k=0 and π, what is Δ(k)=2iΔ sin k?
steps.hint: The sine is zero at these two points.
steps.explanation: Pairing vanishes at these two particle–hole-invariant momenta; ξ determines gap closure.

steps.prompt: What does the sign of ξ(0)ξ(π)=(−2.5)(1.5) imply?
steps.hint: Use this model criterion only with a bulk gap and Δ≠0.
choices: Negative sign, in the nontrivial region
Zero, exactly at the phase transition point
steps.explanation: |μ|=0.5<2t, with a negative sign, belongs to the topological interval of the chain model.

steps.prompt: A pair of near-zero energy appears in a finite open chain, but it is not strictly zero. How should we understand it?
steps.hint: Localized modes at both ends can hybridize over finite lengths.
choices: There must be errors in the code
This directly announced the experimental discovery of Majorana
Possible endpoint hybridization; check the bulk criterion and endpoint weights
steps.explanation: Finite length permits small splitting; assess low-energy spectra, spatial weights, and bulk criteria together.

steps.prompt: Keeping t=1,Δ=0.6, what is the bulk classification after changing μ to 3?
steps.hint: Compare |μ| with 2t.
choices: Unable to classify because Δ is non-zero
steps.explanation: |μ|>2t is the trivial region of this single-channel model. Pairing alone does not establish topology.

exercises.title: Do not impose full index permutation on dynamic χ⁽²⁾
exercises.prompt: Consider χ_ijk(2ω;ω,ω), derive the allowed permutation from the frequency label, and then check 4mm with Oh.

steps.prompt: Which indicator exchange is directly guaranteed by the same two input frequencies?
steps.hint: The output frequency is 2ω and the input frequency is ω.
steps.explanation: Intrinsic permutation acts on the same frequency inputs j and k; there are no additional Kleinman assumptions in this model.

steps.prompt: Do χ_xxz and χ_zxx in 4mm have to be equal?
steps.hint: An exchange involves output indicators.
choices: must be opposites of each other
do not have to be equal, they are independent coefficients
steps.explanation: The three independent coefficients of 4mm are xxz, zxx, zzz.

steps.prompt: How does inversion act on the third-rank polar tensor χ?
steps.hint: Each of the three polar-vector indices contributes a minus sign.
steps.explanation: An odd number of negative signs gives χ→−χ; if the inversion belongs to point group , the invariance condition forces χ=0.

steps.prompt: Bulk electric-dipole SHG vanishes for Oh. Does that mean a real sample can never produce SHG?
steps.hint: The current model has no surface and higher-order multipole contributions.
choices: Yes; it vanishes under every condition
No, processes such as surface and multipole also need to be considered
Only if the incident angle is set to 90° can it be non-zero
steps.explanation: A bulk electric-dipole prohibition does not exclude SHG mechanisms outside the model.

exercises.title: Hand calculation of the relative strength of GaAs (001)
exercises.prompt: According to the agreement on this site, a=χ_xyz=1, θ=45°, and φ=45° are used, and the common strength unit is used.

steps.prompt: What does PS channel mean?
steps.hint: The first letter on this site is incident and the second letter is analyzer.
choices: Two photons P and S respectively
steps.explanation: Channels are input and output polarization labels, not independent polarizations of the two input photons.

steps.prompt: What is A_PP=−cos²θ sinθ sin2φ equal to here?
steps.explanation: Multiplying the three terms gives −1/(2√2).

steps.prompt: What is the corresponding I_PP=|A_PP|²?
steps.hint: Find the amplitude first, then take the square of the modulus.
steps.explanation: Relative intensity is 1/8; it is not calibrated absolute optical power.

steps.prompt: How does the relative strength change when all χ are multiplied by 3 simultaneously?
steps.hint: Amplitude is linear in χ, and intensity is its squared modulus.
choices: unchanged, because the graph is always normalized
steps.explanation: The current module preserves common units without channel-by-channel normalization, so square scaling can be checked directly.

exercises.title: Reverse question: There is more than one explanation for the same picture
exercises.prompt: Look at a graph of angle strength and decide, step by step, which conclusions are supported by the data and which require additional evidence.

steps.prompt: What is the relationship between χ and −χ calculated independent intensity maps?
steps.hint: The corresponding amplitudes are opposite to each other.
steps.explanation: I=|A|² is not sensitive to the overall sign change, and the intensity alone cannot restore the phase.

steps.prompt: 4mm (001) The angular spectrum of the ideal model is constant. Can it be said that the crystal has continuous rotational symmetry?
steps.hint: Finite-order tensors may not see all of the discrete point group information.
choices: Yes; a constant plot can come only from a continuous group
No; this tensor and geometry cannot distinguish them
Yes, as long as the measuring range is 360°
steps.explanation: The symmetry of the angular spectrum may be higher than that of the crystal complete point group and cannot be directly equated.

steps.prompt: GaAs (001) normal incidence Full channel zero, what is the most reasonable explanation?
steps.hint: Td No inversion, but the geometric projection can be zero.
choices: All tensor coefficients are mathematically forced to zero
The current geometric extinction cannot determine the inversion alone.
steps.explanation: It is also possible that a non-zero allowed tensor does not produce a projectable signal in the chosen geometry.

steps.prompt: Which added information is most straightforward to distinguish between two candidates for which only the overall χ changes sign?
steps.hint: To distinguish A from −A requires amplitude-phase sensitivity.
steps.explanation: Phase references provide information missing from intensity measurements; practical modeling still requires dealing with optical boundary conditions.

exercises.title: Momentum folding of N=4 supercell
exercises.prompt: Take a one-dimensional single-orbital chain with a=1 and N=4 primitive cells per supercell, initially without defects.

steps.prompt: supercell reciprocal lattice What is the size of the vector?
steps.hint: The real space period is increased from 1 to 4.
steps.explanation: G_SC=2π/N=π/2; The first Brillouin zone width is equal to this value.

steps.prompt: primitive cell k=3π/4 What is K after folding back [−π/4,π/4)?
steps.hint: can subtract an integer number of π/2; the right endpoint is not in the selected half-open interval.
steps.explanation: 3π/4−2(π/2)=−π/4; ±π/4 are the same physical Brillouin-zone boundary point.

steps.prompt: Does drawing a perfect chain as four folded branches imply four new physical orbitals?
steps.hint: only replaces the calculation cell and does not change the Hamiltonian.
choices: No, it is a relabeling of the same physical spectrum
Yes; enlarging a cell always creates new orbitals
Yes, structural phase change must occur
steps.explanation: The supercell matrix's four intracell orbitals come from four primitive cells; they are not newly created primitive-cell orbitals.

steps.prompt: After unfolding, what should the summed spectral weight of a perfect chain recover?
steps.hint: compares the primitive cell dispersion of ε₀−2t cos k.
choices: Any four curves of equal strength
primitive cell dispersion and its Bloch weight
steps.explanation: expansion reorganizes the same set of energies with spectral weights, and a perfect chain should restore the primitive cell spectrum.

exercises.title: Two-site projection and weight conservation
exercises.prompt: takes N=2 and K=0, the normalized state is c=(1,1)/√2, and the projection factor is exp(−ikj)/√N.

steps.prompt: In k=0, how are the projection amplitudes of the two sites combined?
steps.hint: The two phases are the same; the outer 1/√2 must be included.
choices: adds up to √2, with a weight of 2
adds up to 1 and has a weight of 1

steps.prompt: At k=π, the phase of j=1 is −1. What is W(π) at this time?
steps.hint: Two equal major terms cancel.
steps.explanation: The projection of the uniform state in the alternating momentum directions is zero.

steps.prompt: keeps |c₀|²=|c₁|²=1/2 and changes c₁ to a negative sign?
steps.hint: The real space probability remains unchanged, but the relative phase changes.
choices: eigenstate must not be normalized to unity
steps.explanation: Phase determines momentum projection; site-by-site probabilities or eigenvalues alone cannot reconstruct unfolded weights.

steps.prompt: If a numerical algorithm rotates an eigenbasis within a degenerate energy, which quantity is more suitable for comparison?
steps.hint: Degenerate subspace projection does not rely on internal basis selection.
choices: The weight of any eigenvector must be exactly the same
Only look at the sign of each eigenvector
Merged spectral weights of the same energy subspace
steps.explanation: The weight of individual states is variable, and the combined spectral function is the basis invariant of this degenerate subspace.

exercises.title: Limits and inverse inference in defect spectra
exercises.prompt: first compares the periodic impurity model of N=4, and then looks at the vacancy model that actually deletes an orbital.

steps.prompt: What does one impurity in an N=4 supercell represent in an infinite periodic calculation?
steps.hint: supercell is repeated periodically by Bloch.
choices: Every 4 primitive cell Repeated Impurity Array
steps.explanation: cycle supercell is not the infinite dilution limit, and the cell size needs to be changed to examine the effects between defects.

steps.prompt: After actually removing one orbital, M=3. What is the weight summed over all bands at fixed k?
steps.hint: reference primitive cell is still N=4, and the projection normalization uses 1/√N.
choices: 1, the missing part must be filled in
steps.explanation: Σn W_n(k)=M/N=3/4; the missing spectral weight follows explicitly from orbital counting.

steps.prompt: only has POSCAR and energy band eigenvalues. Can the general expansion weight be reconstructed in this tool?
steps.hint: projection requires complex wave functions and phase convention .
choices: can be automatically allocated according to the energy size.
Yes, set all bands to the same brightness
No, wave function or equivalent complete projection information is required
steps.explanation: Energies lack the required phase and orbital information; the tool does not invent wavefunctions.

steps.prompt: Both dimerization and alternating potentials may open gaps. How should we judge if we only see gaps?
steps.hint: Multiple Hamiltonian mechanisms can produce similar phenomena.
choices: The mechanism cannot be uniquely determined, and additional evidence such as structure/orbit is needed.
steps.explanation: The inverse problem requires comparison of candidate models with additional observables, and the unfolded spectrum itself is not the full ARPES intensity.

cases.title: square lattice electron model: from D₄h representation to energy gap node
cases.summary: Switch constant s, extended s, d and complex d+id on the same normal state dispersion and observe whether the node intersects the Fermi surface.
cases.assumption: A single orbital, spin-singlet pairing, and an input pairing amplitude. There is no self-consistent pairing mechanism or material Tc prediction, and this is not directly identified with a particular cuprate.

cases.title: Kitaev chain: bulk criteria and finite-chain endpoint weights
cases.summary: Compares μ=0.5 and μ=3, observing the bulk energy gap, open chain low energy spectrum, and localization at both ends.
cases.assumption: Spin-free nearest neighbor chain, non-specific nanowire material model; near-zero energy does not equal experimental discovery Majorana, finite size can produce endpoint hybridization.

cases.title: GaAs: Td tensor and crystal-cut dependence
cases.summary: connects the existing zinc blende structure, phonon with the tensor case, comparing (001)/(111) and the four polarization channels.
cases.kind: Real material symmetry background + teaching parameters
cases.assumption: Use a Td-allowed tensor with original teaching χ coefficients. Only bulk electric-dipole geometric response is included, without Fresnel effects or measured intensities.

cases.title: BaTiO₃: Ferroelectric 4mm with complex coefficient interference
cases.summary: follows the phase transition, domain, physical-property tensor route into SHG, comparing the independent coefficients and the observable consequences of the overall sign inversion.
cases.kind: Real material symmetry background + teaching parameters
cases.assumption: A tensor model for the tetragonal 4mm phase, without calculating transition temperatures or actual optical coefficients. Candidates differing only by an overall sign of χ are indistinguishable in independent intensity plots.

cases.title: Si context: centrosymmetric bulk and nonzero surface signals
cases.summary: Use the Oh zero-tensor reference to understand bulk electric-dipole prohibition and why real surface signals do not contradict it.
cases.assumption: Diamond Si bulk point group background is Oh; this preset only verifies the bulk electric dipole zero response and does not calculate the silicon surface, electric quadrupole or actual reflection spectrum.

cases.title: Periodic impurity chains: spectral weights of translational symmetry breaking
cases.summary: Gradually increase the impurity potential and observe how primitive cell momentum weights disperse from perfect chains to multiple branches.
cases.assumption: One-dimensional single orbital orthogonal basis, defect repeats every N primitive cell , not an isolated defect or a quantitative prediction of real doped materials.

cases.title: Dimerization and alternating potentials: different reasons for similar openings
cases.summary: Compare two microscopic perturbations, then test spectral-weight sum rules with the vacancy preset that actually removes an orbital.
cases.assumption: Similar gaps do not uniquely identify mechanisms. Current unfolding weights omit photoemission matrix elements and are not full ARPES intensities.

cases.title: Real VASP data: leaving the wave function in the calculation process
cases.summary: Organize compatible primitive/supercells, k paths, wavefunction outputs, and unfolding postprocessing. First verify phases and normalization with a perfect chain.
cases.assumption: The current site processes one-dimensional orthogonal-orbital JSON data only. It does not read WAVECAR directly or implement general three-dimensional VASP unfolding. Actual tasks can follow a local easyunfold workflow.
